reviews.text: Loved the demo and now the full game has so much more! Can't wait to keep playing it!

Beggar's Road is a small game that overplays its difficulty. Having not followed this game in its development, I went in with low (5 dollar game) expectations, and those expectations were met. The game is small in that I can feel that the developers want to explore more intricate relations between the factions and expand more on the moral quandaries that you may face but there's simply not enough substance to get these relations and difficulties across to the player. The overplaying of difficulty was not something I went in expecting. I had thought I would be playing a ball-crushing simulator where you throw a character after character against a wall until you eventually break through it. Instead, despite my very minimal knowledge of the game, I managed to accomplish basically every achievement in one life that one could, outside of joining the faction opposing the faction I chose to join. (I have not lived to day 150, nor have I won 20 battles. I have accomplished the main questline before day 150 and the amount of random battle encounters there are is shockingly low. I do not feel the need to grind for these achievements. If there are further things that can occur following the main quest, I have not found them despite wandering around the map.) Also, despite the whole beggar shtick, classism doesn't bar you from anything as far as I could tell. As such, you're never really desperate enough to resort to crime, which defeats the purpose of the story the game is trying to tell I believe. I believe the game would be improved by making crime more profitable. Despite my attempts to engage in a beggar's typical employ, I never once succeeded in any of my skulduggery. Either I'm horribly unlucky, or crime truly doesn't pay (and actually forces you to pay.) Additionally, I would like to be able to sell my ill-gotten gains from combat for more than one coin each, and be able to engage in more acts of common banditry. I would like more difficulty options as well. Especially regarding the economy. As it stands, the economy is super easy. Starving to death feels like a matter of forgetting to buy food, rather than a consequence of your own poor decisions. This is mainly because food is ridiculously easy to get, and so is money. Turns out that all those animals in them there woods are edible. Getting ♥♥♥♥-smacked by the local thug population would also be a nice change of pace, but I'm pretty sure I've just been getting lucky with the dice. Speaking of dice, I'm all for gambling. Love gambling. I would love to bet more at a time. In terms of the core parts of gameplay, the writing is enjoyable if a rather bit robotic sounding, the art is much the same. Assuming honesty in the AI disclaimer, the writers and artists should work a bit more on originality in writing and style. The art especially in the little banners for random encounters looks very AI adjacent. The writing is kinda samey and repetitive, and everyone talks the same. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but there are a lot of key phrases that are said over and over again. (Such as, "...in the way that a..." but that's just one that I locked in on, it may not even be overused.) Despite everything I've said, the game is fun. Its interesting exploring the world and meeting new characters, and, for about 10 minutes, you could trick yourself into thinking the world is as dark and grim as the developers make it out to be. After those 10 minutes, you're kicking some serious ass and that's also fun. The game is 6 dollars, and I got 2 hours of fun out of it. That's better fun to cost ratio than a bar. Once it goes off sale, it'll still be better fun to cost ratio than a bar.

If only there was a mid review option. Anyways, price point is decent for what the game gives. I wouldn't really say there's much to replay here. The text is basic, the story is basic, there's no real impact from your choices. The various renown, morality, and faction reputation doesn't really have much of an impact on the game. It's not difficult by any margin, and there's not really anything you need to think about combat wise. Very straightforward Stat vs Stat combat, with a die that can vary 1-8(?), with equipment giving raw bonuses. Decent enough game to kill a few hours I guess.
Why not... my rating is 55 of 100. For 6 bucks, quick one evening game, its ok.
Very short and a bit too easy, but a fun game non the less.

I liked it and it was fun in a choose-your-adventure style. This game wasn't difficult for the sake of being difficult like 'Heads Will Roll'. Yes, there is RNG to contend with but I liked how it is game-friendly RNG that is meant for fun, not for punishment for buying the game (HWR). I wish I could create my own character but I liked how my pre-made character died but the game didn't end because I had another person in my small party of two. So, the game continued because it wasn't a complete party wipe. I completed the game with that second person as the new leader while my party grew to the max of four persons. I recommend this as a nice distraction type of game if you don't have a day to spend gaming.
Easy on click game,with several quest & story line you can folow. Price = okay.
stuck with random characters, stats and perks, extremely slow and boring then die due to a random encounter you should win having superior armor and weapons.
For the price its really not a bad game, it was enjoyable. I hope dev add more content to it.
Fun and simple
content is so poor, just so so...
I really enjoy this game.

4 hours of play time; Its a simple game, but if you like the ad video from the store page you will probably enjoy the game. With that said- I probably wont play more than I have because its a little repetitive. *If they add more towns or more experiences I think it could be a great game. Worth the $10 I spent on it.
Very cool game. Worth the price.

[table] [tr] [th]游戏由SteamPY鉴赏家提供[/th] [/tr] [tr] [td]SteamPY鉴赏家[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][h3]上SteamPY淘海量超低价游戏[/h3][/td] [/tr] [/table] 本作是一款由Coldframe Studios独立制作并发行的中世纪肉鸽类型游戏，游戏剧情背景设定在中世纪末期1407年的列日地区，这里位于佛兰德地区，处于列日主教治下，但现在因为纠纷和战乱，整个列日地区被三种势力瓜分，玩家扮演的主角是一个一无所有的乞丐，不仅要在城镇、森林与被遗忘之地之间游荡，更是要在这个残酷、琐碎、偶尔荒诞的世界中挣扎求生！ 游戏玩法是肉鸽向的文图冒险类型，有存读档的机制，硬核程度不高，现阶段游戏内容尚有所欠缺，可游玩内容比较重复，玩家要在不同地区游荡以及和当地人搞好关系来接任务委托，但是要注意的是，一但支持一方，就会得罪另一方，或许可以尝试在三者之间保持平衡。 游戏中主角团队移动地点和过夜都会消耗食物，住宿在有些地区都需要消耗钱币，刚开局可以乞讨维生，但不能长久，最好的办法是来到列日的酒馆，一顿赌博便可当场破局，好甲好剑、充足的食物、属性优秀的队友以及战斗难度急剧下降的敌人等等这些问题都在金钱面前解决了。 总的来说游戏现阶段内容只支持浅玩，游玩两小时基本可以体验全内容，深度向机制根本没有，充其量只能算是一个简单的中世纪模拟器，好在价格便宜，感兴趣的小伙伴可以等游戏完善后再入手体验一番。

TLDR: Demo has the entire game. I played the demo and thought it was pretty fun, I liked how easy it is to die, how at the start you really feel liek you're scrounging around as a beggar. There are like three areas blocked off which i assumed meant there were going to be a bunch more quests and more content with the characters I'd already met. So i bought the full game. There was not. I think there are like 3 more characters which means three more quests and also 1 more faction. but my issue with this game is that after you get a good sword and plate armor you steam roll through every encounter. also I'd done all the quests by turn 100 which meant it was 50 turns till the next story event and then 150 to the one after that which was super boring. Maybe if I hadn't played the demo I could have squeezed two hours of content out of the game, but i really felt like I only got an hour of actual enjoyable gameplay out of this, which is sad because what is here is decently fun. Hopefully the creator will add more story or characters to fill some of the late game space or at least make the battle towards the end of the game much more challenging.
Fun to play, although short. Worth the price. Could easily handle an expansion.

Got this as a gift. I would advise that people do not purchase this as a gift. Quest lines are broken, the game feels soulless, dialogue is constantly recycled in an effort to pad out interactions. User interface options often route to the same function. AI was used in every facet of the creation of this game. It is my personal belief that replies on the community page also seem to be AI as they are all formatted in the same structure. NPC pictures are good, but inconsistent in style. "Trying your luck" with people seems to be a screen fade to black, but other than a chance to be wounded, does not seem to do much. Buying a round at the tavern only ever effects your loyalist reputation, though you drink with commoners only. If you don't mind the overt use of AI, then go in knowing that quest lines are broken, screen resolution cannot be changed, the UI is janky, combat loot drops do not depend on enemy type, and the honor meter does not mean very much. Play the outlaw route and you'll watch the game break itself in real time if you're not regularly going out of your way to rob civilians. The whole thing is soulless. Honestly this game just makes me sad.

I wish it was actually a roguelike and you could buy improvements for each run. Or that your could choose anything about your character. Or that you didn't start in the same spot for each run. For $5, it's not a bad game. Just overpromised
Um, not bad. Lots of RNG, but interesting concept. Might be a good game here in the future, but I'd recommend waiting to see where they go with this.

Well, it felt promising. I liked the thought of the game as it was presented and the game has potential. It's just that it lacks.. flavor, intrigue, content, possibillities, difficulty. It is not what it says it is. It is also very heavily AI "crafted". Or at least that is the taste you get in the mouth.. And then, there is the end. Just, no. You play a game, that could be done by day 150, easy. And the end comes at day 250, wether you like it or not. You have done all for one of the sides and what you have done has absolutely no influence over the end. None what so ever. I might look back at the game later, but I might just as well forget it ever was.

Not worth the time. I did two runs in under two hours and on the second one beat the game. Very easy if you can play the dice game at the tavern. You can on Day 1, amass more money than you will ever need, max out your Virtue, and buy the best weapon in the game "Good Sword" as well as the best armor, Full Plate. (Though buy the Chain Shirt until you have the Strength to actually carry the sword and the full plate at the same time.) So you have effectively removed any challenge from the game at that point. Unlimited coin, food, the best gear which makes losing combat unlikely. You can buy up to 3 more companions and equip them the same to basically guarantee it. Though I didn't even need to, I just got one. Unfortunately you will quickly realize the gambling game in the tavern is the most thought out and fun portion of the game, and its just Liar's Dice. Except its bugged and will only give you certain options to claim instead of the one you want. (And yes I know you have to bid higher, but if the opponent says 3 Daggers, sometimes claiming 4 Daggers is simply not an option for no apparent reason. Though I suspect its just a limited number of 'dialogue' responses can be displayed so it drops some.) The art is AI crap and the dialogue is also AI crap.

This game scrapes by the skin of its' teeth for me. I am a bit dubious that the game was not made with more AI than what's it's saying it was. However, as I cannot prove it everything from here on out is with the assumption that everything that was made was largely done by human hands. So the game is a very short tale about going out into the world as a beggar and working your way up while settling certain disputes and then eventually successfully completing your story with a faction going from there. If you play this game like a roguelike I think you get way more value out of it than if you save scum it. It makes all of the choice more impactful, and battles more tense. The problem is that these game needed more. More of pretty much everything. More story, more choices, more combat. However, as I picked it up for $5 I am not going to complain too much. However, if you haven't played games like Roadwarden before go spend your money on that instead. Final Grade C-

Not really worth it imo. Cute enough and a fun concept, but too easy to hit the point where you steamroll everything and also you hit what is effectively the 'win' condition WAY too quickly, and after that it's just repeating the same stuff over and over, endlessly amassing money you don't even need and can't do anything with.

This one lands at Neutral for me. I expected something like Roadwarden and although this game is a fun choose your own adventure story, it's certainly no Roadwarden. I played for a few hours alongside my husband and we completed the story and most of the achievements on the first run which only took a few hours (breaks included) so the game is quite short. The Developers mention that the art is AI rendered which is certainly obvious but I actually like it, I think the Baroque like art style looks really nice. No mention if the writing had some help from AI but there were some inconsistencies in the stories in places. One example.. I went into a tavern and talked to the people there. The barmaid said "My Father is dying upstairs, so I'm running the place." I then turned to another lady who said the girl's father is dead already. (That was quick!) There are encounters as you travel the map. The one with the upturned cart occurred three times in the same run so there seems to be a lack of variety there. I wish there was more to it. More story, a bigger map, more characters, more encounters. I feel it's got the bare bones of a decent game but could do with a lot more fleshing out. I'm glad I got it at a reduced price because I think upwards of £7 for this is a bit much for what you get. I did get something really special from this game though. I got a lovely evening with my husband that felt like we were back playing our homebrew rpg game together , something we did before our little children were born with him as the GM and me as the player immersed in the world he created for us. This time we were following someone else's story and making decisions together but it brought back that same feeling for me and that's why I wish I could have more time with it. Final word- best to grab it on sale but worth a shot .

I enjoyed this game immensely... Except that it's far too short and there are quite a few bugs in how the quests are handled. Most of them don't appear to be game breaking, though there are reports of quest-lines getting bugged out. Regardless, it was a fun experience with my only complaint being that I want more expansive maps, longer quest lines, and overall just more of the world to explore. It's got good bones, but even on a complete playthrough it feels a bit "Demo" like.
I like it.
Scratches the Cute Knight itch.

Seems like a decent game all in all but I've now tried 10 different times to make progress as different characters and keep dying in stupid situations. Any time you die you have to start from the very beginning and play through the same story beats over and over making it wildly monotonous. I just died in another run where I had not only plate armor but the best sword I could afford (+4) damage and still died to someone with 1 strength and 2 defense. Basically, buy this game if you're fantastic at dealing with monotony, if not then find something else.

I recently purchased Beggar's Road based off of a YouTube stream I watched and largely enjoyed a play through. The game is fun and has intriguing and sometimes frustrating mechanics (in particular Beggar's Bluff game). All said and done though, for $7.99, its a good buy and a nice entry point. The standard difficulty is very easy though so I'd recommend ramping it up. The overall game took me roughly 5 hours which is pretty quick. I mean I believe I can keep going as it didn't truly "end." It more just said I achieved the highest status. I'd love to say a Beggar's Road 2 at some point or a healthy DLC to expand the base-game because I could see myself playing this more. Its just complicated enough to be fun and the personalities you interact with seem unique and different. No idea how it will feel on a second or third playthrough and if everything meaningfully changes tho. All in all for $7.99 (and price is determining score), I'd give this an 7/10. -1 for being too short, -1 for a very limited map, -1 for not enough of walkthrough -specifically on Beggar's Bluff, and -1 for being very basic. + 3 For the characters (NPCs not your team), +2 for the events, +2 for the impact of your decisions, and + 3 the combat, and +1 for being less than $10.00.
